name: Hugging Face / Transformers
bestFor: Model research, semantic correctness, calibration, and embedded Python applications.
recommendedToday: Selected Context or embedded Native Memory
benefit: Use the transparent reference path to validate routing, positions, model topology, and memory behavior before moving into a production serving engine.
why: Transformers provides the clearest mechanism surface and broad model-family access for controlled qualification.
worksWithoutModification: PRA SDK selects ordinary prompt or message context.
Exact source records remain outside the model request.
Fallback broadens or disables selection without changing the engine.
nativeOpportunities: Reuse immutable selected resources as layer-native model memory.
Calibrate model-family topology and position behavior.
Transfer qualified profiles into production serving integrations.

evidence.summary: Reference mechanism and PRA-off compatibility paths are validated on pinned research configurations; serving economics are not the purpose of this runtime.
evidence.engineVersion: Pinned research environments; website export does not carry one universal version
evidence.workload: Mechanism, routing, model-family, and compatibility probes

limitations: Routing quality remains model- and domain-dependent.
Serving throughput and tail latency require a serving-engine benchmark.
A reference result is not automatically a production recommendation.
deploymentExample: Application → PRA SDK selection → Transformers generate()

qualification.nextGate: Re-run the target model, domain, hardware, and quality harness before promotion.

partnerOpportunity: Use this path to onboard a model family or establish the semantic control for another engine.

name: MLX / MLX-LM
bestFor: Local AI and unified-memory inference on Apple Silicon.
recommendedToday: Selected Context; Native Memory when qualified
benefit: Reduce visible context immediately, then evaluate reusable native memory where repeated prefill and unified-memory pressure make it relevant.
why: MLX exposes memory tradeoffs directly on Apple Silicon and supports a practical local qualification path.
worksWithoutModification: Gateway or SDK selection feeds normal MLX-LM prompts.
No model retraining is required.
Selected Context remains the ordinary-text fallback.
nativeOpportunities: Reuse selected immutable resources as native memory.
Separate semantic memory from rotating sequential cache.
Measure unified-memory residency and transfer together.

evidence.summary: Selected Context and Native Memory mechanisms are validated. Synchronized larger-model results place native execution near Selected Context parity at scale, not at a universal dramatic speedup.
evidence.workload: Matched Selected Context and Native Memory qualification

limitations: Native gain depends on model, selection, reuse, and memory pressure.
Near-parity results must not be represented as a universal speedup.
Re-run on the exact Mac, model, and workload before choosing native execution.
deploymentExample: Local application → PRA selection → MLX-LM Selected Context; optionally qualified Native Memory

qualification.nextGate: Publish versioned workload rows with latency, memory, and quality provenance.

partnerOpportunity: Extend controlled qualification across larger models and production-shaped local workloads.

name: vLLM
bestFor: High-throughput open-model serving on NVIDIA infrastructure.
benefit: Selected Context can reduce context pressure without changing vLLM; deeper work tests whether reusable non-prefix memory improves matched serving economics.
why: vLLM is a common production choice where compatibility value can be measured before scheduler integration.
worksWithoutModification: PRA Gateway sends selected ordinary messages or prompt text.
vLLM prefix caching remains independent.
Fallback uses the same OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
nativeOpportunities: Attach request-local, geometry-matched non-prefix memory.
Coordinate immutable reuse with prefix caching.
Qualify concurrency, isolation, warm residency, and scheduler ownership.

evidence.summary: Selected Context has strong context-pressure evidence. Native CUDA correctness, concurrency, and isolation are promising; matched native-HOT and native-WARM economics remain under qualification.
evidence.engineVersion: Research branch; versioned product row pending
evidence.workload: Matched context-pressure, correctness, concurrency, and serving probes

limitations: Native serving economics are not yet a production claim.
Warm-tier transfer and reuse need matched measurements.
Tenant and session isolation must remain explicit under concurrency.
deploymentExample: Application → PRA Gateway Selected Context → existing vLLM OpenAI endpoint

qualification.nextGate: Close matched native-HOT/native-WARM quality, latency, throughput, and isolation rows.

partnerOpportunity: Jointly qualify native memory, cache coexistence, and scheduler lifecycle on a production-shaped fleet.

name: SGLang
bestFor: Advanced serving, RadixAttention, and hierarchical cache research.
benefit: Compose exact prefix reuse with semantic-resource selection while keeping their identities and accounting separate.
why: SGLang exposes cache and scheduler mechanisms suited to prefetch and hierarchical residency research.
worksWithoutModification: PRA sends selected ordinary context.
RadixAttention continues exact prefix reuse.
Semantic records remain outside SGLang’s public wire format.
nativeOpportunities: Prefetch selected immutable memory.
Separate semantic-resource identity from radix-prefix identity.
Measure scheduler, distributed, and off-node lifecycle economics.

evidence.summary: Native mechanism and prefetch evidence exists. Scheduler-owned, distributed, and off-node economics remain the next qualification boundary.

limitations: Distributed and off-node economics are not yet promoted.
Prefix and semantic resource identities must not be conflated.
Native serving remains a partner qualification path.
deploymentExample: Application → PRA Gateway Selected Context → SGLang endpoint

qualification.nextGate: Measure scheduler-owned residency, transfer, tail latency, and useful throughput.

partnerOpportunity: Jointly qualify prefetch and hierarchical residency without changing radix-prefix semantics.

name: OpenVINO GenAI / OVMS
bestFor: Intel CPU, GPU, NPU, Windows, edge, and enterprise deployments.
benefit: Reduce ordinary input context before OpenVINO generation while preserving a conventional deployment and fallback.
why: OpenVINO reaches enterprise, edge, Windows, and Intel hardware environments beyond CUDA-first serving.
worksWithoutModification: PRA Gateway or SDK selects ordinary text.
Existing OpenVINO GenAI or OVMS interfaces remain the engine boundary.
No detached native-memory claim is required.
nativeOpportunities: Investigate documented engine-owned cache seams only when supported.
Measure batching and device-memory effects against Selected Context.
Keep any future native path capability-negotiated.

evidence.summary: Updated controlled results support Selected Context as the recommendation. The current evidence does not establish detached Native Memory support.
evidence.workload: Selected Context compatibility and controlled inference

limitations: Do not infer detached native-memory support from ordinary cache behavior.
Device-specific serving economics require a versioned target configuration.
Broader CPU, GPU, and NPU coverage remains ongoing.
deploymentExample: Application → PRA Gateway Selected Context → OpenVINO GenAI or OVMS

qualification.nextGate: Publish versioned model, Intel device, quality, latency, and memory rows.

partnerOpportunity: Qualify Selected Context across Intel deployment profiles and identify an explicit native seam only if upstream supports it.

name: NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM
bestFor: NVIDIA-centric deployments focused on optimized production inference.
benefit: Measure semantic selection alongside paged memory, prefix reuse, batching, connectors, and disaggregated serving without conflating identities.
why: TensorRT-LLM is a priority path for NVIDIA fleets with strict latency and throughput goals.
worksWithoutModification: PRA sends selected ordinary context through the existing endpoint.
Prefix reuse and paged memory continue under engine ownership.
Fallback remains the same model-serving route.
nativeOpportunities: Map selected resources into explicit connector and paged-memory seams.
Qualify disaggregated transfer and reuse.
Attribute engine scheduling gains separately from selection gains.

evidence.summary: Selected Context is the current recommendation. Native-memory and native-serving economics remain ongoing and are not presented as production gains.
evidence.workload: Matched Selected Context, connector, and serving qualification

limitations: No production-qualified native connector profile is published.
Disaggregated transfer economics remain workload-specific.
Versioned quality and serving rows are still required.
deploymentExample: Application → PRA Gateway Selected Context → TensorRT-LLM endpoint

qualification.nextGate: Close versioned connector lifecycle, quality, latency, throughput, transfer, and isolation results.

partnerOpportunity: Qualify connector-backed Native Memory and Native Serving on a production-shaped NVIDIA topology.

name: AirLLM
bestFor: Feasibility experiments where model weights exceed accelerator memory.
benefit: Reduce selected text without adding another request-path streaming cost to an already bandwidth-constrained workload.
why: AirLLM exposes the hard case where weight streaming and context-memory movement compete for the same resources.
worksWithoutModification: PRA selects ordinary input context before AirLLM generation.
The public Transformers-compatible path remains the boundary.
Fallback does not require native memory movement.
nativeOpportunities: Reduce request-path preparation overhead.
Coordinate weight and context transfer schedules.
Re-test only when the cost model predicts a credible reuse win.

evidence.summary: Native Memory is technically feasible in the research integration, but current request-path overhead outweighs reuse benefit for the tested workload.

limitations: Current native overhead fails the promotion gate.
Weight and context streaming compete for I/O bandwidth.
Predictable production latency is not established.
deploymentExample: Application → PRA Selected Context → AirLLM / Transformers-compatible generation

qualification.status: Native path blocked by measured overhead
qualification.nextGate: Demonstrate lower preparation and transfer cost than the reuse benefit on a frozen workload.

partnerOpportunity: Optimize coordinated streaming and use the negative baseline as the explicit promotion threshold.

name: llama.cpp
bestFor: Portable GGUF inference across desktops, edge devices, and heterogeneous hardware.
benefit: Reduce ordinary input context across llama.cpp deployments without changing GGUF model execution.
why: llama.cpp offers broad local and edge reach with a familiar server and CLI boundary.
worksWithoutModification: PRA Gateway targets the OpenAI-compatible server.
PRA SDK can assemble selected prompts for CLI or library calls.
Normal slot and prompt-state features remain engine-owned.
nativeOpportunities: Define an explicit GGUF-compatible non-prefix memory seam.
Validate position and model-geometry behavior.
Keep semantic-resource identity distinct from slot persistence.

evidence.summary: Selected Context is the recommended compatibility path. Normal slot or prompt-state persistence is not PRA Native Memory; explicit GGUF-native work remains an integration opportunity.
evidence.model: Not yet pinned for native qualification
evidence.workload: Selected Context compatibility; native seam not yet qualified

limitations: Slot persistence must not be relabeled as semantic Native Memory.
No explicit native GGUF result is promoted.
Hardware backends require separate measurement.
deploymentExample: Application → PRA Gateway Selected Context → llama.cpp server

qualification.nextGate: Pin a model, backend, native seam, workload, and matched quality-cost benchmark.

partnerOpportunity: Design and validate an explicit GGUF-native semantic-memory interface.

name: Ollama
bestFor: Simple local model distribution and OpenAI-compatible application development.
benefit: Stop replaying all documents and history while keeping Ollama as the local application endpoint.
why: Ollama is a widely used application-facing local model surface where compatibility should stay simple.
worksWithoutModification: PRA Gateway selects ordinary messages for Ollama’s compatible endpoint.
No model retraining or Ollama patch is required.
Fallback sends ordinary selected or full text.
nativeOpportunities: Delegate deeper behavior only to a backend that advertises it.
Negotiate capability and invalidate state on reload or model switch.
Validate the backend path independently.

evidence.summary: Selected Context through the Gateway is the recommendation. Deeper native behavior should be delegated only to a backend that explicitly advertises and validates it.

limitations: Ollama-level state is not automatically PRA Native Memory.
Backend reload and model-switch invalidation require explicit testing.
No live native performance claim is published.
deploymentExample: Existing application → PRA Gateway Selected Context → Ollama endpoint

qualification.nextGate: Version compatibility, reload, reconnect, model-switch, and backend capability tests.

partnerOpportunity: Add explicit capability advertisement and validate a backend-native path without duplicating engine ownership.

name: FreeToken
bestFor: Joint semantic-context and bandwidth-adaptive serving research.
benefit: Study how semantic selection and bandwidth-aware serving policies can share an explicit cost model.
why: FreeToken is a research path for coordinating what context is useful with when and where reusable state should move.
worksWithoutModification: Use ordinary Selected Context as the control.
Keep semantic selection independent of any serving claim.
Retain exact records and a text fallback.
nativeOpportunities: Coordinate semantic selection with bandwidth prediction.
Test prefetch and placement policies.
Attribute selection and serving gains independently.

evidence.summary: This is joint semantic-context and bandwidth-adaptive serving research. No live native performance claim is published yet.
evidence.workload: Joint semantic and serving qualification to be defined

limitations: No live native result is published.
The serving interface and benchmark configuration remain under definition.
Research direction is not a deployment recommendation.
deploymentExample: Baseline application → PRA Selected Context control → research serving integration

qualification.nextGate: Pin the engine, model, hardware, workload, semantic control, and serving metrics.

partnerOpportunity: Co-design a frozen-selection benchmark for bandwidth-aware prefetch and placement.
